text:
Alex: alert fired -> 429_spike_by_org in us-west. ~12% 429s over last 10m, mostly from org_894. Link: https://datadog.internal/redwood/alerts/13421
Maria: seen it, thanks. is this bursty (token bucket) or real quota enforcement? p95 latency looks fine so maybe burst credits
Jess: runtime emits token_bucket_remaining but at 1m granularity. we might be missing short drains on busy keys
Rahul: CS-oncall here — getting customer messages. can we triage quickly and avoid noisy notifications if it's a single org?
Alex: quick triage notes:
- top offender: api_key=org_894_key (60% of 429s)
- routes: /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings
- observed pattern: high short-term request bursts from a single key, then 429s start after ~30s
Maria: ok. proposing two-monitor strategy:
  A) Burst monitor (short window) -> page SRE only if > X keys causing >10% 429s in last 2m
  B) Sustained monitor -> page and create incident if >5% 429s across >3 orgs for 15m
Alex: example Datadog burst monitor (copy/paste):
```
avg(last_2m):anomalies(avg:service.http.429{env:prod}.as_count(), "basic", 2, direction="above", alert_window="last_2m", interval=30)
```
PromQL alternative (per-org 429% over 5m):
```
100 * sum by(org) (rate(http_requests_total{status="429"}[5m])) /
(max(1, sum by(org) (rate(http_requests_total[5m])))) > 5
```
Jess: dashboard panels we should add:
- real-time 429% (1m / 5m) per-org
- token_bucket_remaining avg and p50/p95 per-key (10s sample)
- top 10 keys by 429s and by RPS
- routes heatmap showing which endpoints exhaust fast
Maria: telemetry work: I'll add sampling for token_bucket_remaining at 10s for top 10k keys and surface a derived metric burst_credit_drain_rate per key
Rahul: CS playbook patch (short):
1) Check dashboard -> confirm top affected orgs
2) If single org -> contact CS owner, ask for client-side throttling
3) If multi-org or sustained -> page SRE, open INC and notify affected customers
4) If due to internal load (backfill/batch) -> apply temporary routing throttles or increase burst allowance for Dedicated customers
Alex: runbook steps for SRE when monitor fires:
- Check top keys panel
- Look at token_bucket_remaining and recent token refills
- Correlate with deployments / traffic anomalies (deploy-bot / logs)
- If it's a single misbehaving key, temporarily throttle at edge and DM CS
- If system-wide, trigger capacity escalation and fallback to lower-cost model variants
Jess: I'll add the burst monitor and dashboard panels today. ETA 4h for initial monitors, 48h for sampling rollout
Maria: I'll ship the sampling change and create an event that flags top keys for higher-res telemetry. ETA 24-36h
Rahul: I'll update the CS template + canned message and be ready to contact org_894
Alex: created INT-2893 to track follow-ups (dashboards + monitors + runbook). assigned to Jess/Maria/Rahul. tagging SRE-Bot to post updates
SRE-Bot: acknowledged. Linked INT-2893 into the incident tracker. Will post status updates every 30m until resolved :white_check_mark:
quota-bot: auto-note: current per-key burst config = token_rate=100/s, burst_capacity=300. Consider lowering burst or adding sliding-window detection for noisy keys :warning:
Maria: quick question — should we add a metric for %keys_with_0_tokens? that would let us alert before many users are affected
Alex: yes, add that to sustained monitor criteria
Rahul: thumbs up from CS. I'll reach out to org_894 in parallel and pause any noisy jobs if they agree
Jess: starting monitor work now. ping me if you want to test with a synthetic key
Alex: thanks team. please update INT-2893 with any action. closing Slack thread for now, will reopen if monitor pages or INT escalates :thumbsup:
